blocks.text: For one long second, the whole office goes quiet. The bag of green beans sags. You have just told your new [[对门|duìmén|across the hall]] neighbour, in front of the [[物业|wùyè|property management]] clerk, that you do not eat. Ever. Her eyes travel from your face to your wrists, measuring exactly how thin you are, already planning a rescue.

blocks.h: 不吃？！你不吃饭？哎呀，这怎么行！
blocks.p: Bù chī?! Nǐ bù chīfàn? Āiyā, zhè zěnme xíng!
blocks.e: You don't eat?! You don't eat meals? Oh my, how can that be!

blocks.text: Help comes from an unlikely direction. The gate guard has wandered in to refill his thermos, and he has heard everything. He does not smile. He points the thermos at you like a teacher's pointer and translates you back into a functioning adult. [[还没|hái méi|not yet]]: not yet. Not never.

blocks.p: Tā shì shuō, hái méi chī. Ǹg.
blocks.e: He means he hasn't eaten yet. Mm.

blocks.h: 哦，还没吃啊！早说嘛！走，吃面去！
blocks.p: Ò, hái méi chī a! Zǎo shuō ma! Zǒu, chī miàn qù!
blocks.e: Oh, you haven't eaten YET! Why didn't you say so! Come on, let's go get noodles!

blocks.text: By noon the noodle shop at the gate is a sauna with plastic stools. [[张阿姨|Zhāng āyí|Auntie Zhang]] steers you in by the elbow and announces to the room that the [[新来的|xīn lái de|newcomer]] in 501 has not eaten. At "501" the owner's ladle pauses for half a beat, exactly like the clerk's pen did this morning. Then the grin is back.

blocks.p: Liǎng wèi! Yào là de ma? Jǐ liǎng?
blocks.e: Two of you! Spicy? How many liang?

blocks.text: Auntie Zhang orders for you: two liang, spicy, extra greens because you are "too thin". The noodles arrive glowing red, and they are, as promised, [[巴适|bāshì|really good]]. Your lips go numb. Your nose runs. You have never been happier. Then she remembers: no [[电卡|diànkǎ|electricity card]] means no lights, no fan and no fridge tonight. She marches you back across the courtyard, past the guard's booth, where you notice a small chipped bowl of water set neatly by the door. You haven't seen a single dog in the [[小区|xiǎoqū|housing compound]].

blocks.p: Diànkǎ! Mǎi diàn! Wǒ gēn tā shuō!
blocks.e: Electricity card! Buying power! I'll tell her!

blocks.p: Āyí, ràng tā zìjǐ shuō ma.
blocks.e: Auntie, let him say it himself.

blocks.h: 五零一的电卡。买多少钱的？
blocks.p: Wǔ líng yāo de diànkǎ. Mǎi duōshao qián de?
blocks.e: The card for 501. How much do you want to buy?

moment.prompt: Tell her you want a hundred yuan's worth.

opts.note: 块 (kuài) is the everyday word for yuan, and 的 (de) makes it "a hundred yuan's worth".
r: Hǎo, yìbǎi kuài de. Děng yíxià.
Okay, a hundred yuan's worth. One moment.

opts.note: Add 块 (kuài) after the number so it is clear you mean money: 一百块的.
千 (qiān) is a thousand; a hundred is 百 (bǎi), so say 一百块的.
r: Yìqiān?! Nǐ yào yòng dào míngnián ma?
A thousand?! Are you planning to use it until next year?

summary: Your '我不吃' horrifies 张桂芳 until gruff 周大勇 explains you mean 还没吃; she drags you to 刘志强's noodle shop for a spicy midday lunch (his ladle pauses at '501', and you spot a water bowl by the guard's booth though there are no dogs), then marches you to the property office to buy power on your electricity card, where the clerk makes you say the amount yourself.
